rounds.title: Starter pairs 1

clues: A long-legged wading bird
A machine used to lift heavy loads
cards.example: The ____ swung the steel girder onto the roof.
cards.explanation: A crane is a long-legged wading bird, and also a machine with a long arm for lifting heavy loads.

clues: The sound a dog makes
The outer covering of a tree trunk
cards.example: The dog began to ____ at the postman.
cards.explanation: A bark is the sharp sound a dog makes, and bark is the rough outer covering of a tree trunk.

clues: The underside of a foot
A type of flatfish
cards.example: We had grilled Dover ____ with lemon.
cards.explanation: The sole is the underside of the foot, and a sole is a flatfish.

clues: A sporting contest
A small stick used to start a flame
cards.example: She struck a ____ to light the candle.
cards.explanation: A match is a sporting contest, and also a small stick that bursts into flame when struck.

clues: A long structural piece of timber
A narrow shaft of light
cards.example: A ____ of sunlight fell across the table.
cards.explanation: A beam is a long piece of timber used in building, and also a narrow shaft of light.

rounds.explanation: Each answer has both independently clued senses.
fixtureHints: Card b has an animal sound and a tree meaning.

rounds.title: Starter pairs 2

clues: The land at the edge of a river
A business that holds deposits of money
cards.example: They had a picnic on the grassy ____ of the river.
cards.explanation: A bank is the land alongside a river, and a business that keeps money for customers.

clues: The season between winter and summer
A coiled elastic piece of metal
cards.example: The daffodils flower in early ____.
cards.explanation: Spring is the season between winter and summer, and a spring is a coil of metal that returns to shape.

clues: A marine mammal
To close something so it is watertight
cards.example: Press the lid down firmly to ____ the jar.
cards.explanation: A seal is a marine mammal, and to seal something is to close it so nothing can get in or out.

clues: A flying mammal
An implement used to hit a ball in cricket
cards.example: The ____ hung upside down in the barn.
cards.explanation: A bat is a flying mammal, and the wooden implement used to hit the ball in cricket.

clues: A sweet preserve made from fruit
A blockage of road traffic
cards.example: We were stuck in a traffic ____ for an hour.
cards.explanation: Jam is a sweet fruit preserve, and a traffic jam is a blockage of vehicles.

rounds.explanation: The answers are BANK, SPRING, SEAL, BAT and JAM.
fixtureHints: Card c can be a noun or a verb.

rounds.title: Gentle pairs 1

clues: A band worn on a finger
The sound a telephone makes
cards.example: She wore a gold ____ on her finger.
cards.explanation: A ring is a band worn on the finger, and the sound a telephone makes when a call comes in.

clues: The inside of the hand
A tropical tree with large fan-shaped leaves
cards.example: Hold the coin flat in the ____ of your hand.
cards.explanation: The palm is the inner surface of the hand, and a palm is a tropical tree.

clues: A round citrus fruit
The colour between red and yellow
cards.example: She peeled an ____ for her packed lunch.
cards.explanation: An orange is a citrus fruit, and orange is also the colour between red and yellow.

clues: It opens a lock
One of the black or white levers on a piano
cards.example: He turned the ____ and the door swung open.
cards.explanation: A key opens a lock, and the keys of a piano are the levers pressed to play notes.

clues: A water bird with a flat bill
To lower your head quickly to avoid being hit
cards.example: A ____ and her ducklings swam across the pond.
cards.explanation: A duck is a water bird, and to duck is to bob down quickly out of the way.

rounds.explanation: Gentle cards pair two concrete, everyday meanings.

rounds.title: Gentle pairs 2

clues: A small rodent with a long tail
A device moved by hand to point on a computer screen
cards.example: Click the left button on the ____ to open the file.
cards.explanation: A mouse is a small rodent, and the hand-held device that moves the pointer on a computer.

clues: The hard covering at the tip of a finger
A thin metal spike hammered into wood
cards.example: Hammer the ____ into the fence post.
cards.explanation: A nail covers the tip of each finger and toe, and a nail is a metal spike driven in with a hammer.

clues: A racket sport played indoors against walls
A fruit drink diluted with water
cards.example: Would you like orange ____ or water?
cards.explanation: Squash is a racket game played in a walled court, and a concentrated fruit drink you dilute with water.

clues: The main woody stem of a tree
An elephant's long nose
cards.example: The elephant lifted the log with its ____.
cards.explanation: A trunk is the main stem of a tree, and an elephant's long flexible nose.

clues: A field where football or cricket is played
To put up a tent
cards.example: We found a flat spot to ____ the tent.
cards.explanation: A pitch is a sports field, and to pitch a tent is to put it up.

rounds.explanation: Gentle cards pair two concrete, everyday meanings.

rounds.title: Gentle pairs 3

clues: A device that blows cool air
An enthusiastic supporter of a team
cards.example: Switch on the ____; it is sweltering in here.
cards.explanation: A fan moves air to cool a room, and a fan is also a keen supporter.

clues: A knot tied with two loops
A weapon that shoots arrows
cards.example: Tie the ribbon in a neat ____.
cards.explanation: A bow is a decorative knot with two loops, and a curved weapon for shooting arrows.

clues: A stick used to hit a golf ball
A group of people who meet for a shared interest
cards.example: She joined the local book ____.
cards.explanation: A golf club is used to hit the ball, and a club is also a group of people with a shared interest.

clues: The hard outer case of an egg or snail
An explosive fired from a large gun
cards.example: The snail pulled back into its ____.
cards.explanation: A shell is the hard outer case of an egg, snail or nut, and an explosive projectile fired from artillery.

clues: A strip of cloth worn round the neck with a shirt
A result in which both sides have the same score
cards.example: He wore a striped ____ to the interview.
cards.explanation: A tie is worn knotted at the collar, and a tie is a result where the scores are level.

rounds.explanation: Gentle cards pair two concrete, everyday meanings.

rounds.title: Gentle pairs 4

clues: The front of the body between the neck and the stomach
A large strong box for storing things
cards.example: The old sea ____ was full of blankets.
cards.explanation: The chest is the front of the upper body, and a chest is a large sturdy box.

clues: A unit of British money
A unit of weight equal to sixteen ounces
cards.example: The bag of flour weighs one ____.
cards.explanation: The pound is the UK's unit of currency, and a pound is also a weight of sixteen ounces.

clues: A small sticker put on a letter to pay the postage
To bring your foot down hard
cards.example: Put a first-class ____ on the envelope.
cards.explanation: A stamp pays for postage, and to stamp is to bring your foot down heavily.

clues: A character of the alphabet
A written message sent by post
cards.example: She wrote a ____ to thank her grandmother for the present.
cards.explanation: A letter is a character such as A or B, and a written message sent in an envelope.

clues: A moving ridge of water on the sea
To move your hand to say hello or goodbye
cards.example: A huge ____ crashed onto the beach.
cards.explanation: A wave is a moving ridge of water, and to wave is to move your hand in greeting.

rounds.explanation: Gentle cards pair two concrete, everyday meanings.

rounds.title: Standard pairs 1

clues: An early version of a piece of writing
A written order for a bank to pay a sum of money
cards.example: This is only the first ____ of my speech.
cards.explanation: A draft is a preliminary version of a document, and a banker's draft is an order for a bank to pay money. In British English both are spelt DRAFT; the air-current sense is DRAUGHT.

clues: The price asked for something
To rush forward to attack
cards.example: There is no ____ for children under five.
cards.explanation: A charge is the price asked, and to charge is to rush forward in attack.

clues: A strip used for measuring and drawing straight lines
A king, queen or other person who governs
cards.example: Draw the margin with a ____.
cards.explanation: A ruler measures and rules straight lines, and a ruler is a person who governs a country.

clues: A flow of water, air or electricity
Belonging to the present time
cards.example: The ____ swept the boat downstream.
cards.explanation: A current is a flow of water or electricity, and current means happening now.

clues: The place where someone is buried
Serious and worrying
cards.example: The doctor's face was ____ as she gave the news.
cards.explanation: A grave is a burial place, and grave means serious and solemn.

rounds.explanation: Standard cards pair a concrete meaning with a more abstract one, with tighter wording.

rounds.title: Standard pairs 2

clues: Treating everyone equally
An outdoor event with rides and stalls
cards.example: The children rode the carousel at the ____.
cards.explanation: Fair means just and even-handed, and a fair is a travelling show with rides and stalls.

clues: The city where a country's government is based
Money used to start or run a business
cards.example: Paris is the ____ of France.
cards.explanation: A capital is the seat of government, and capital is money invested in a business.

clues: Not heavy
What makes it possible to see
cards.example: Turn on the ____; it is getting dark.
cards.explanation: Light means of little weight, and light is the brightness that lets us see.

clues: Able to wait calmly without complaining
A person receiving medical treatment
cards.example: The nurse checked on each ____ in the ward.
cards.explanation: Patient means calm and tolerant of delay, and a patient is someone being treated by a doctor.

clues: Giving out a lot of light
Quick to learn and understand
cards.example: She is a ____ pupil who picks things up quickly.
cards.explanation: Bright means shining strongly, and also clever.

rounds.explanation: Standard cards pair a concrete meaning with a more abstract one, with tighter wording.

rounds.title: Standard pairs 3

clues: Soft and easy to chew
A formal offer to carry out work for a stated price
cards.example: Slow cooking makes the beef beautifully ____.
cards.explanation: Tender meat is soft and easy to cut, and a tender is a formal bid for a contract.

clues: Unwilling to spend or share money
The average of a set of numbers
cards.example: Add the scores and divide by five to find the ____.
cards.explanation: Mean describes someone stingy, and the mean is the arithmetical average.

clues: Something that you hear
In good condition, sensible and reliable
cards.example: That is ____ advice; I would follow it.
cards.explanation: A sound is anything heard, and sound also means solid, healthy or well founded.

clues: Happy and satisfied with what you have
What is inside something
cards.example: The cat was ____ to doze by the fire.
cards.explanation: Content means satisfied, and the content of something is what it contains. The stress moves, but the spelling is the same.

clues: Rising or falling sharply
To soak in liquid to draw out flavour
cards.example: Leave the tea leaves to ____ for three minutes.
cards.explanation: Steep describes a sharp slope, and to steep is to soak something in liquid.

rounds.explanation: Standard cards pair a concrete meaning with a more abstract one, with tighter wording.

rounds.title: Standard pairs 4

clues: A long book telling an invented story
New and unusual
cards.example: What a ____ idea; nobody has tried that before.
cards.explanation: A novel is a long work of fiction, and novel means new and original.

clues: A building where horses are kept
Firmly fixed and not likely to change
cards.example: The patient's condition is now ____.
cards.explanation: A stable houses horses, and stable means steady and unlikely to change.

clues: A line of seats in a theatre
A noisy quarrel
cards.example: We sat in the front ____ of the stalls.
cards.explanation: A row is a line of seats or things side by side, and a row (rhyming with cow) is a noisy argument.

clues: To say numbers in order
A European nobleman
cards.example: The ____ lived in a castle above the village.
cards.explanation: To count is to say numbers in order, and a count is a European noble, equivalent to an earl.

clues: To push firmly against something
Newspapers and journalists as a group
cards.example: The minister refused to speak to the ____.
cards.explanation: To press is to push steadily, and the press means newspapers and reporters collectively.

rounds.explanation: Standard cards pair a concrete meaning with a more abstract one, with tighter wording.

rounds.title: Expert pairs 1

clues: A cold current of air in a room
A flat round piece moved diagonally on a chequered board
cards.example: Shut the door; there is a terrible ____.
cards.explanation: A draught is a current of air indoors, and one of the pieces in the game of draughts. British spelling: DRAFT does not fit either meaning.

clues: A blow with a closed hand
A mixed fruit drink served from a large bowl
cards.example: Ladle some ____ into everyone's glass.
cards.explanation: A punch is a blow with the fist, and punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl.

clues: A large wicker basket with a lid
To hold back or obstruct
cards.example: Heavy rain will ____ the rescue effort.
cards.explanation: A hamper is a lidded wicker basket, often for food, and to hamper is to hinder.

clues: A short period of time
Words believed to have magical power
cards.example: We enjoyed a sunny ____ in early March.
cards.explanation: A spell is a short period, as in a dry spell, and a magic spell is a form of words with supposed power.

clues: Equipment for fishing
To deal with a difficult task
cards.example: It is time to ____ the pile of paperwork.
cards.explanation: Fishing tackle is the angler's gear, and to tackle a problem is to deal with it.

rounds.explanation: Expert cards use less obvious, established senses and restrained misdirection.

rounds.title: Expert pairs 2

clues: An enclosed area containing a group of buildings
To make a bad situation worse
cards.example: Arguing with the referee will only ____ the problem.
cards.explanation: A compound is a fenced area with buildings, and to compound a problem is to make it worse.

clues: A piece of cloth with a design, flown from a pole
To become tired or less lively
cards.example: By the last mile the runners began to ____.
cards.explanation: A flag is flown as a symbol, and to flag is to tire or weaken.

clues: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders
Having run out of money; bankrupt
cards.example: The firm went ____ after losing its biggest customer.
cards.explanation: A bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders, and a business that goes bust is bankrupt.

clues: Pellets of ice falling from the sky
To call out to attract attention, as to a taxi
cards.example: She stepped to the kerb to ____ a cab.
cards.explanation: Hail is falling ice, and to hail someone is to call out to them.

clues: Firmly fixed so that it will not move
To go without food
cards.example: Many people ____ from dawn to sunset during Ramadan.
cards.explanation: Fast means securely fixed, as in stuck fast, and to fast is to eat nothing for a time. The clue avoids the obvious 'quick'.

rounds.explanation: Expert cards use less obvious, established senses and restrained misdirection.

rounds.title: Expert pairs 3

clues: The pointed end of something
A place where rubbish is taken and dumped
cards.example: We took the old sofa to the ____.
cards.explanation: The tip is the pointed end, and in British English a tip is a rubbish dump.

clues: An evergreen conifer
Neat and smart in appearance
cards.example: He looked very ____ in his new suit.
cards.explanation: A spruce is a conifer, and spruce means neat and trim.

clues: A building used for worship
The flat side of the head beside the eye
cards.example: She rubbed her ____ as the headache began.
cards.explanation: A temple is a place of worship, and the temple is the side of the forehead.

clues: A place where coins are made
In perfect, as-new condition
cards.example: The stamp album is in ____ condition.
cards.explanation: The mint produces coins, and mint condition means as good as new. The herb sense is a deliberate distraction.

clues: Rubbish that is thrown away
To say that you will not do something
cards.example: Collect the ____ bags from the kerb on Tuesday.
cards.explanation: Refuse (stress on the first syllable) is waste, and to refuse (stress on the second) is to decline.

rounds.explanation: Expert cards use less obvious, established senses and restrained misdirection.

rounds.title: Expert pairs 4

clues: To leave someone stuck with no way of leaving
A single thin thread or hair
cards.example: A ____ of hair fell across her face.
cards.explanation: To strand someone is to leave them stuck, and a strand is a single thread or hair.

clues: A skilled activity making things by hand
A boat, aircraft or spacecraft
cards.example: The small ____ drifted towards the harbour.
cards.explanation: A craft is a skilled trade, and a craft is also a vessel for travel by water, air or space.

clues: A person who mends shoes
A baked fruit pudding with a scone topping
cards.example: Take your boots to the ____ to be resoled.
cards.explanation: A cobbler repairs shoes, and a cobbler is a fruit pudding topped with scone dough.

clues: A garden tool with a row of prongs
A fashionable man who lives an immoral life
cards.example: Use a ____ to gather up the fallen leaves.
cards.explanation: A rake gathers leaves, and a rake is also a dissolute man of fashion, as in The Rake's Progress.

clues: To hit hard and repeatedly
A mixture of flour, eggs and milk
cards.example: Whisk the ____ until it is smooth, then fry the pancakes.
cards.explanation: To batter is to strike repeatedly, and batter is the mixture used for pancakes and fried fish.

rounds.explanation: Expert cards use less obvious, established senses and restrained misdirection.
